thread_title: Find a post from the last 3 days: Waking up at 3 or 4 AM every night and can't fall back asleep
thread_summary: Look for someone describing early waking without a medical diagnosis or medication question.
text: Early waking often has boring causes worth ruling out first: alcohol in the evening (it wears off in the second half of the night), caffeine after early afternoon, a warm room, or going to bed so early that your sleep need is met by 3 AM. If you wake, keep the lights and phone off, and if you're still awake after about 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light until you feel sleepy. A fixed wake time, even after a bad night, builds sleep pressure for the next one. If it has gone on for weeks alongside low mood, it's worth raising with a doctor.
why: 3 AM waking is one of our quiz answers and a core Nights pain point. Careful sub, so behavioural only.
format: Comment bank (pick a post from the last 3 days)
rules: NON-NEGOTIABLE: reply only to a thread posted in the last 3 days (check the timestamp under the title). If nothing that recent fits, skip this comment and mark it Rejected with a note. Prefer threads with few comments, adapt the first line to what OP actually said, and add no links and no pitch. Check the r/sleep sidebar before commenting.
